edges.description: Functional lysosomal hydrolase deficiency leads to multisystem substrate accumulation.

edges.description: Multisystem storage in connective tissues and cartilage produces the severe skeletal and soft-tissue phenotype.
Multisystem storage affects cardiac valves, mucosa, and the thoracic cage, producing cardiorespiratory disease.
Multisystem lysosomal dysfunction is associated with cessation of neuromotor development.
Craniofacial soft-tissue storage produces coarse facial features.
Gingival connective-tissue storage produces gingival hypertrophy.
Skeletal storage produces dysostosis multiplex and deformed long bones.
Severe skeletal storage disease contributes to cessation of statural growth.
Skeletal storage produces thoracic deformity and kyphosis.
Dermal connective-tissue storage produces thickened skin.
Cardiac valve thickening and insufficiency manifest as valve disease.
Airway narrowing and thoracic-cage stiffening manifest as respiratory insufficiency.
Neuromotor developmental arrest manifests clinically as global developmental delay.

Loss of the catalytic alpha/beta subunits abolishes phosphorylation of high-mannose oligosaccharides on acid hydrolases, which is the molecular lesion the node names, and the mistargeted hydrolases appear in serum.
edges.limitations: A gene-trap null models the severe ML II end of the GNPTAB allelic spectrum; it does not address the residual-activity genotypes that produce ML III alpha/beta.

edges.description: Storage-type cytoplasmic changes appear in exocrine secretory cells and cartilage is defective, but the organ distribution does not match human ML II.
edges.limitations: Severe retinal degeneration dominates the mouse phenotype, whereas human ophthalmic data in ML II are limited and retinal degeneration is not a defining feature of the human disease; the paper frames the retina as the study's focus rather than as a validated human correlate. Organ-by-organ storage burden should not be transferred from this model to patients.

nodes.description: Biallelic GNPTAB variants abolish GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase, preventing formation of the mannose-6-phosphate marker that targets soluble acid hydrolases to the lysosome. Untagged enzymes are missorted and hypersecreted rather than delivered, leaving the lysosome functionally deficient in multiple hydrolases.

nodes.description: Gene-trap disruption of the alpha/beta subunit precursor of GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase, the enzyme mutated in ML II. Homozygotes are small, have cartilage defects, cytoplasmic alterations in exocrine secretory cells, severe retinal degeneration, and elevated serum lysosomal enzymes. This model is the clearest available demonstration of why enzyme amount and enzyme activity are separate observations: the hydrolases are *raised* in serum because they are secreted instead of delivered to the lysosome, while mannose-6-phosphate tagging - the activity that routes them - is abolished. MGI annotates the same gene on both MP branches accordingly (MP:0001570 abnormal circulating enzyme level; MP:0005584 abnormal enzyme/coenzyme activity).
Growth often ceases in the second year of life.
